concepts.name: Fourier transform
concepts.definition: An integral transform that takes a function as input and outputs another function describing the extent to which various frequencies are present.

concepts.name: Frequency domain representation
concepts.definition: The output of the Fourier transform that describes the decomposition of a function into its frequency components.

concepts.name: Integral transform
concepts.definition: A mathematical operation that transforms a function using an integral formula.

concepts.name: Uncertainty principle (time-frequency)
concepts.definition: Functions localized in time domain have transforms spread in frequency domain and vice versa; fundamental tradeoff between time and frequency localization.

concepts.name: Gaussian function
concepts.definition: A critical case for uncertainty principle; its Fourier transform is also a Gaussian, important in probability theory and physics.

concepts.name: Fourier series
concepts.definition: A variant of Fourier analysis for periodic functions, expressing them as sums of sine and cosine terms.

concepts.name: Dirac delta function
concepts.definition: A generalized function used in Fourier analysis and signal processing, whose Fourier transform is the constant 1.

concepts.name: Complex sinusoid
concepts.definition: A function of the form e^(i*theta) combining amplitude, phase, and frequency in a single complex exponential.

concepts.name: Tempered distribution
concepts.definition: A generalized function that extends the Fourier transform to cases beyond Lebesgue-integrable functions.

intuitions.text: Musical chord analogy: The Fourier transform decomposes a signal like decomposing a musical chord into its constituent pitches with their relative intensities.
Time-frequency tradeoff: A function concentrated in time is spread in frequency, and vice versa - you cannot simultaneously pinpoint exact time and exact frequency.
Frequency domain view: Instead of thinking of a signal as a function of time, the Fourier transform lets you see it as a composition of frequencies.
Frequency extraction: Multiplying by a complex exponential at frequency xi has the effect of checking if that frequency is present - only the matching component produces a non-zero integral.
Problem-solving strategy: Some difficult problems become easier in the frequency domain; the Fourier transform provides a different perspective that simplifies mathematical manipulation.
Dual representations: Every signal has two equivalent representations - one as a function of time, another as a function of frequency - related by the Fourier transform.
Domain duality: The time domain and frequency domain are dual spaces - the units must be inverse (seconds vs. hertz), and neither is more fundamental than the other.
Wave duality: In quantum mechanics, particles can be described in position space or momentum space, connected by the Fourier transform - both perspectives are equivalent.

applications.use: Converting differential equations to frequency domain simplifies solving them algebraically, then inverse transform recovers time-domain solution.
Relating position and momentum representations of wave functions; essential for quantum mechanics formalism.
Analyzing, filtering, and processing signals by examining their frequency content.
Analyzing spectral data in chemistry, physics, and astronomy.
Natural framework for studying waves in physics and engineering.

properties.name: Linearity
properties.statement: The transform of a linear combination equals the linear combination of the transforms

properties.name: Time shifting
properties.statement: Shifting in time introduces a linear phase shift in frequency

properties.name: Frequency shifting
properties.statement: Multiplication by complex exponential shifts frequency content

properties.name: Time scaling
properties.statement: Scaling in time inversely scales frequency

properties.name: Symmetry
properties.statement: Decomposing complex functions into real/imaginary and even/odd parts creates symmetric relationships under transform

properties.name: Conjugation
properties.statement: Transform of complex conjugate relates to transform at negative frequencies

properties.name: Plancherel's theorem
properties.statement: Total energy of a signal is preserved under the transform

properties.name: Convolution theorem
properties.statement: Convolution in time becomes multiplication in frequency

properties.name: Cross-correlation theorem
properties.statement: Cross-correlation in time relates to multiplication in frequency domain

properties.name: Differentiation
properties.statement: Time-domain differentiation becomes frequency-domain multiplication by frequency

chronology.label: Fourier publishes theory of heat
chronology.detail: Fourier claimed any continuous or discontinuous function can be expanded into a series of sines - foundation for modern Fourier analysis.

people.name: Joseph Fourier
people.role: Introduced sine and cosine transforms in study of heat transfer; developed foundational Fourier analysis methods.

relatedTransforms.name: Discrete Fourier transform (DFT)
relatedTransforms.relation: Finite discrete version for sampled signals (group = Z mod N)

relatedTransforms.name: Discrete-time Fourier transform (DTFT)
relatedTransforms.relation: Discrete version for infinite sequences (group = Z)

relatedTransforms.name: Fourier series
relatedTransforms.relation: Variant for periodic functions (group = S1, unit circle)

relatedTransforms.name: Fast Fourier transform (FFT)
relatedTransforms.relation: Efficient algorithm for computing the DFT in O(n log n) time

relatedTransforms.name: Sine and cosine transforms
relatedTransforms.relation: Real-valued variants corresponding to imaginary and real parts of FT

relatedTransforms.name: Laplace transform
relatedTransforms.relation: Related transform extending FT to complex half-plane for stability analysis

examples.description: Piano chord frequency analysis: Fourier transform of a C major chord waveform shows fundamental frequencies (C, E, G) as peaks, with higher-frequency overtones as smaller peaks.
Frequency detection example: Real and imaginary parts of the integrand at different frequencies show how the transform measures presence of each frequency component.
